items.title: Ex-trainer van Club Brugge maakt op 71-jarige leeftijd opvallende comeback langs de lijn
items.summary: Adrie Koster is op 71-jarige leeftijd opnieuw trainer. De Nederlander, die in België vooral bekend is als voormalig coach van Club Brugge, gaat aan de slag bij het Schouws elftal. Dat gelegenheidsteam bestaat uit amateurvoetballers uit de regio en treedt regelmatig aan tegen profclubs in de voorbereiding.

items.title: Rondje Eredivisie Extra: 'Defensief moet de lat omhoog bij PSV'

items.title: David Silva (40) naar Hong Kong: 'Ze brachten het alsof het voor een jaar is'

De komst van de Spanjaard werd woensdag wereldkundig gemaakt. Silva is blij met dat nieuws, maar voegde wel toe dat de supporters zich geen illusies hoeven te maken.

items.title: 'Italië geeft gas voor EK 2032: nieuwe stadions in Milaan en Rome'
items.summary: A C Milan en AS Roma hebben goed nieuws gekregen richting de bouw van een nieuw stadion voor het EK van 2032. items.title: Vincent Kompany krijgt bijzondere onderscheiding in Beieren: “Hij is een voorbeeld voor onze samenleving”
items.summary: Vincent Kompany heeft in Beieren inmiddels meer opgebouwd dan alleen een sterke reputatie als trainer. Niet alleen zijn sportieve prestaties worden daarmee beloond, maar ook zijn duidelijke engagement tegen racisme.

items.title: Vincent Kompany reçoit un nouveau prix et un grand honneur : "Un avocat engagé de l'humanité"

items.title: Eckert’s Spygate ban may be lenient, but no sane manager will try the same trick again
items.summary: Verdict has been a long time coming and the Southampton head coach has recaptured hearts and minds at St Mary’s “Hi Tonda, are you a cheat?” That simple, succinct, question cut to the heart of a matter that has vexed the Football Association all summer. It was posed by the Northern Echo’s Dominic Shaw after Southampton overcame Middlesbrough in the second leg of May’s Championship playoff semi‑final and proved the cue for Tonda Eckert to walk out of his press conference at St Mary’s. Although Southampton’s manager subsequently admitted to authorising spying on opponents, England’s football authorities struggled to decide what punishment best fitted an act some regard as heinous but which others fail to take seriously. Now, in autumn, we finally have an FA verdict, with Eckert given a six-week ban suspended until the end of the 2027-28 season, a £28,000 fine and a reprimand. Continue reading...

items.title: All aboard the Tuchel train? England camp has clear winners and losers
items.summary: While it’s full steam ahead for Alex Scott, Lewis Hall and Myles Lewis-Skelly, others look likely to be left behind Thomas Tuchel’s original idea had been for continuity. The England manager wanted to build on the positives from the World Cup and he was minded to stand by the vast majority of the players who had been a part of the journey to the semi-finals in North America over the summer. His squad for the four-match Nations League window and the beginning of a new international cycle would not be defined by radical change. What was it about the best-laid plans? As Tuchel prepared to name his group in mid-September, he knew that he would be without a clutch of World Cup players because of injury. He then lost another handful after the announcement. Fast forward to the Czechia game at Wembley on Tuesday night – the final one of the quartet – and, after further withdrawals, Tuchel could count only 12 players who were available to him during the World Cup. He knows the train moves quickly in football, stopping for nobody. That flexibility is a prerequisite in his line of work. This felt like something else. Continue reading...

items.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
items.summary: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team, she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘I wanted to depart in the best way possible’: Kieran McKenna on Ipswich exit and future plans
items.summary: In an exclusive interview, former Ipswich manager talks of his lasting affection for the club, savouring time out with family and friends and ideas for his next move It was on the Portman Road pitch, bathed in bright early May light while immersed in the relief and joy of a third promotion in five years, that Kieran McKenna realised the moment was right. The thought had flickered earlier in the season that this might be his final campaign at Ipswich, only to be pushed into the subconscious by the Championship’s remorseless grind. “But standing out there, I felt this was probably time,” he says of those moments after QPR had been swept aside and a return to the Premier League assured. “Another big victory, a full stadium, in front of my family and the fans. It was an amazing way to go out on a high.” Five months later McKenna has no regrets about electing to cut things short while the going was so good. The golf bag lying outside his garage speaks of a man enjoying the break and, more pertinently, of something bigger. His son has recently become interested in the sport and sharing those moments with loved ones, whether out on the greens or spending part of the summer travelling along the East Anglian coastline in a camper van, were among the biggest reasons to pause a soaring career. At 40, McKenna had spent two decades immersed in coaching; it was time to appreciate life’s essentials while continuing professional development at his own speed. Continue reading...
